name: Doxycycline
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Unlike other tetracyclines, doxycycline needs no dose change in kidney impairment: its half-life is similar in normal and severely reduced kidney function, because elimination shifts away from the kidney. Hemodialysis does not change its half-life.
kidney_function_basis: Label PK uses CrCl (mL/min); no dose bands.

bands.recommendation: No dose change: usual doses do not accumulate excessively in kidney impairment, and the half-life (18 to 22 hours) is similar in normal and severely impaired kidney function (label).

dialyzable: No: dialysis does not alter serum half-life (label).
monitoring: Photosensitivity; intracranial hypertension symptoms (headache, vision); BUN rise is reported with tetracyclines but not with doxycycline in kidney impairment (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: Children; avoid during tooth development (under 8 years) except for severe or life-threatening infections such as anthrax or Rocky Mountain spotted fever (label warnings).
pediatric.usual_dose: Under 45 kg, severe or life-threatening infections: 2.2 mg/kg every 12 hours. Over 8 years and under 45 kg, less severe disease: 4.4 mg/kg divided into 2 doses on day 1, then 2.2 mg/kg daily (once or divided). 45 kg or more: adult dose (label).
